Solid refactor: replacing per-test `services_mock.<svc> = Mock(<Svc>)` boilerplate with a single annotation-driven `create_services_mock()` removes a large amount of duplication and keeps service mocks spec'd. I verified the mechanics against the stdlib: `Mock(spec=<class>)` yields `AsyncMock` children for `async def` methods (unittest.mock `_spec_asyncs`), so awaiting mocked service methods still works, and annotated names are set with `setattr` (plain `spec`, not `spec_set`, allows that).

Issues worth addressing:
- The MR description says `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock` now supports pool permissions, but the class is unchanged: `__getattr__` returns `item in self._permissions`, i.e. a bool, for `list_pools_with_view_machines_access` / `list_pools_with_view_available_machines_access`. Handlers do `set(await fga_client.list_pools_...)`, so the auth-only machines test only passes because any non-401/403 status is accepted (it actually 500s).
- The new per-endpoint setup added to `TestMachinesApi.endpoints_with_authentication_only` is dead code: the test body calls `mocked_api_client_user_with_permissions()`, which overwrites `openfga_tuples.get_client.return_value` afterwards. Also `get_client` is a sync method, so `fga_client` there is a `MagicMock` and those configured methods would not be awaitable anyway.
- `@pytest.mark.filterwarnings("ignore:coroutine ... was never awaited")` masks a signal that usually means an async service call wasn't awaited; the repo's `[tool.pytest]` only escalates `BytesWarning`, so this filter also looks unnecessary. Better to fix the mock return values (e.g. always install `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock` for `get_client`) than to silence it.
- Type-hint migration is incomplete: `create_app_with_mocks` / `create_internal_app_with_mocks` still annotate `mocked_services: ServiceCollectionV3` although every caller now passes `Mock`.
- Minor: the loop over `ServiceCollectionV3.__annotations__` assumes annotation values are runtime classes; `typing.get_type_hints(ServiceCollectionV3)` is more robust (stringized annotations/non-class aliases would break `Mock(service_class)`), and eagerly instantiating ~77 spec'd mocks per test has measurable cost (`Mock(spec=...)` does `dir()` + signature introspection per class). Lazy creation in a `Mock` subclass would keep the de-duplication without the per-test cost.

I did not execute the suite (no shell available in this review environment); findings are from static inspection of the merged tree and the full diff.

src/tests/fixtures/__init__.py.66: This eagerly builds ~77 `Mock(spec=<ServiceClass>)` instances for every test that uses `services_mock`. `Mock(spec=...)` introspects `dir()` and the class signature per service, so this adds per-test overhead across the suite where previously children were created lazily on access. Consider lazy creation (e.g. a `Mock` subclass that instantiates `Mock(service_class)` on first attribute access) to keep the de-duplication without paying for unused services.
src/tests/fixtures/__init__.py.71: Relying on raw `ServiceCollectionV3.__annotations__` assumes the annotation values are runtime classes. That holds today (no `from __future__ import annotations` in `maasservicelayer/services/__init__.py`), but it silently degrades to `Mock('<string>')` if stringized annotations are ever enabled or if a non-class annotation (e.g. `Annotated[...]`, alias) is added. `typing.get_type_hints(ServiceCollectionV3)` is the robust equivalent.

src/tests/maasapiserver/fixtures/app.py.106: Type-hint migration is incomplete: `create_app_with_mocks(mocked_services: ServiceCollectionV3)` (line 41) and `create_internal_app_with_mocks(mocked_services: ServiceCollectionV3)` (line 84) still declare `ServiceCollectionV3`, but every caller now passes the `Mock` returned by `create_services_mock()`. Update those two signatures too; otherwise the change advertises `Mock` while two helpers still require the concrete collection type.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/public/ha.40: Suppressing `RuntimeWarning: coroutine ... was never awaited` here is risky: `Mock(spec=<ServiceClass>)` already turns `async def` service methods into `AsyncMock`, so an un-awaited coroutine in these authorization tests indicates a code path calling an async service without awaiting it (a real bug), not a benign mock artifact as the comment claims. The stated cause is also inaccurate for the MagicMock return values of async service methods. Fix the mock setup (e.g. always install `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock` for `openfga_tuples.get_client`) or the offending handler, rather than filtering; note `pyproject.toml` only escalates `BytesWarning`, so the filter is otherwise unnecessary.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/public/ha.211: These three lines have no effect. `test_endpoints_require_authentication_only` calls `mocked_api_client_user_with_permissions()` inside the test body, which sets `services_mock.openfga_tuples.get_client.return_value = AsyncOpenFGAClientMock(set(permissions))` and overwrites the `fga_client` configured here. In addition, `OpenFGATupleService.get_client` is a synchronous method, so the child created by `Mock(OpenFGATupleService)` is a `MagicMock`; awaiting `list_pools_*` on it would raise `TypeError` anyway. The GET /machines endpoint therefore still fails: `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock.__getattr__` returns a bool for `list_pools_with_view_machines_access`, and the handler does `set(view_access_pools)` -> TypeError -> 500, which the test tolerates because it only rejects 401/403. Either make `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock` return lists for the two pool-list methods (as the MR description implies) or configure the permissions object, not this throwaway MagicMock.
